query: SoftBank ownership stake in Arm and margin loan
normalized: arm loan margin ownership softbank stake

output.content:
- **Ownership:** SoftBank Group remains Arm’s controlling shareholder, owning roughly **86%–90%** of Arm; a May 2026 filing-based figure cited **922.7 million shares, or 86.4%**, held indirectly through its wholly owned Kronos II LLC, while contemporaneous reporting characterized the stake as “almost 90%.” [[1]] [[2]]

- **Margin-loan balance at FY2025 year-end:** At **March 31, 2026**, SoftBank reported **$14.1 billion (¥2.2 trillion)** outstanding under margin loans collateralized by Arm shares. [[3]] [[4]]

- **Borrowing increase during FY2025:** SoftBank’s Arm-share margin borrowing increased by **$11.5 billion** in the year ended March 31, 2026; its consolidated financial report recorded **¥3.1685 trillion** of borrowings using Arm shares at that date. [[5]]

- **Facility versus amount drawn:** The Arm-backed facility had been expanded from **$13.5 billion to $20.0 billion** in November 2025, whereas the March 2026 **$14.1 billion** figure was the outstanding balance—not the full facility size. [[6]] [[3]]

- **Subsequent update:** In September 2026, Bloomberg reported that SoftBank increased the facility by **$5 billion to $25 billion**; it said **$20 billion had been drawn as of December**, the loan matures in **September 2027**, and it was secured by **769 million Arm shares (72% of Arm)** as of May. [[2]]

- **Analytical implication:** SoftBank has retained control of Arm while monetizing part of the stake’s collateral value rather than selling shares, but the structure increases exposure to Arm-share-price volatility and potential collateral/margin requirements. [[2]]
